messages:
Maya (CS): Heads-up — ACME goes live Thursday 09:00 PST. They want streaming responses + aggressive client-side retry. Renewal conversation in 6 weeks; renewal health currently yellow. Can we draft an enablement runbook focused on: seed-cache, micro-batching, stream-handoff, and a lightweight feedback capture flow for PMs? @Ravi @Diego?

Ravi (Eng): I can sketch the runtime checklist. Key items: ensure seed-cache warmed with top 200 prompts, set micro-batch window to 40ms (or 8 reqs) for low-latency high-throughput mix, and enable stream-handoff to fall back to non-streaming variant on degraded KPIs.

Sofi (CS): +1. Also want checkpoints for enablement calls: T-48h (warm group), T-4h (smoke with production keys), T+24h (feedback capture). Who will own the post-launch feedback digest? We should attach a short feedback form link for the PM and CSM.

Diego (SRE): From infra side: schedule a warm-pool for the tenant (reserved slot), set circuit-breaker to 3xx/drop after 30s, and put a temporary rate-limit bump for the go-live window. I recommend these Ops toggles:
```
# temporary go-live toggles
reserved_gpu_pool: acme-warm-1
burst_quota: 2x
circuit_break_threshold: 30s
microbatch_window_ms: 40
seed_cache_keys: top_200_prompts.csv
```

Maya (CS): Nice. For renewal risk we need a monitoring playbook: track 3 signals — latency P95, failed_stream_rate, NPS mention in feedback. If any two spike, trigger weekly AMR and propose a focused enablement workshop.

Noah (ACME): helpful — can we add a lightweight in-product rating after the first 3 interactions? customers hate extra clicks but a single star/emoji seems ok. Will share our top-50 seed prompts by EOD.

Ravi (Eng): Perfect. For the feedback capture, plan: one-line in-app rating -> webhook -> CS Slack channel (cs-feedback) + small transcript snippet. Keep privacy: redact PII server-side. Implementation sketch:
```
POST /v1/feedback
{
  "tenant_id": "acme",
  "rating": 4,
  "snippet": "First message and response (PII redacted)"
}
```

Sofi (CS): I'll own the feedback digest (T+24h summary + T+7d triage). I'll also coordinate the enablement checkpoints and invite a solutions engineer for the T-4h smoke.

Diego (SRE): OpsBot: schedule reservation for acme-warm-1 at 2026-03-26T08:30Z and enable burst_quota.

OpsBot: reservation created -> acme-warm-1 (id: rsv-2387). Burst quota enabled until 2026-03-26T13:00Z.

Maya (CS): Owners recap: Ravi -> runtime checklist + seed-cache config, Diego -> infra toggles & warm-pool, Sofi -> feedback digest + enablement schedule, Noah -> seed prompts. I'll assemble the runbook doc and share a short checklist for the customer-facing enablement (1 page).

Ravi (Eng): Quick micro-runbook bullets I will add to the doc:
- Warm seed-cache (upload CSV to control plane)
- Validate micro-batch window and run batch-sim locally (script: `tools/sim_batch.sh --window 40`)
- Enable streaming with a 500ms initial-token timeout and stream-handoff on 5% degraded tokens
- Smoke test via prod keys: 5 concurrent sessions with the top-10 prompts

Maya (CS): Great — can we all review the runbook draft by EOD tomorrow? If no objections, I'll post a short customer-facing checklist + link to the feedback form in the go-live announcement. :thumbsup:

Noah (ACME): Thanks team — this helps a lot. Quick ask: can stream-handoff be explained in plain terms for our ops team? They prefer a non-technical fallback description.

Sofi (CS): Will do — I'll add a 2-line plain-language note: "If streaming degrades, the system will deliver the full response at once so users still get an answer quickly. Your session stays intact."

Diego (SRE): Added a small observability hook: annotate metrics with `tenant=acme,phase=go_live` for 48h to simplify dashboards.

Maya (CS): Thanks — wrapping up. I'll post the doc link here when ready.
